chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Jam sessions at Nellie Lutcher's house, and Don Byas wiping everyone out
summary: Players gathered at Nellie Lutcher's; Byas made everyone play every tune in every key.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. We just jammed everywhere we could find to jam -- that's you know -- oh, most favorite spot to jam was around Nellie Lutchers house.
She lived right around the corner on old 40th Street from the Downbeat. And she was some kind of piano player. This was before she sang. And you wanted to lock up -- you locked up there.
Who all can you remember jamming at Nellie's?

I can remember these, two tenor players I was telling you about. Bob [Dawes] and Andy Anderson were there and Washington out of Earl Hines band was there. And a trumpet player by the name of Lloyd Hunter and Don Byas come in and wiped out everybody (laughter) because see they were trying to see how many choruses they could play, you know, in jamming and when Don Byas came down here, he changed things around.

Like you had to go through the keys every tune that you played, you had to play it in every key. Every night, he would end up with just him and the drummer on the bandstand (laughter). And he went to Chicago and did this at the Club 'Duluxa' run everybody off the bandstand, he went to New York and did it,
